comment: Cross-business imports the WebUI role check accepts deliberately. Plan §5.3.2 lets a feature import another feature's *approved public* interface; a feature's contracts are its published surface and need no entry, but any other cross-business edge does. Each entry names both files so a reviewer sees the exact dependency, and a `reason` so the next migration can judge whether it should survive. An entry that no longer matches a measured edge fails the check (see `roleRule`), so the list shrinks as ownership transfers instead of accumulating.

entries.reason: The transcript renders the interaction business's plan decision card as the response surface of a plan turn (plan 5.2 transcript row: uses the interaction answer API). The card is that business's own UI. T05 moved the interactions business into `client/features/interactions/` and the path was re-pointed then; the entry goes when interactions publishes the delivery/decision card as a public surface instead of a peer's UI module.

The transcript's message actions build session commands (fork / edit / rewind). Those builders are the sessions business's command shape, filed under its projection until sessions publishes its public command surface; the entry goes when it does (T07).

The unread controller decides whether a session is still working by asking the turn business for its active-turn probe; before the sessions owner moved into features/sessions/ both files sat in the application layer, so the edge was intra-layer. The probe is a turn read that turn has not published as a public contract yet; the entry goes when it does.

Session commands read the turn stream state to decide whether a session is mid-turn before they submit a lifecycle command. Both files were in the application/projection layers before the sessions owner moved, so the edge was intra-layer; it becomes a reviewed peer edge until turn publishes that read.
The same mid-turn decision reads the turn bundle. Reviewed peer edge until turn publishes its contracts.

Archiving or deleting a session clears that session's Composer draft, so the workflow calls the composer store's own clear. Repointed when T13 moved the composer owner into its feature home; the entry goes when composer publishes a public clear command.

The rail's context chip renders the Composer's context breakdown. It is a Sessions rail overlay reading another business's projection; the entry goes when the Composer publishes that read as a public contract (T13 owns the composer surface).
The chip's popover is the Composer's context-usage projection. Reviewed peer edge until the Composer publishes it.
The chip counts the current session's messages, which the Transcript projects. Reviewed peer edge until the Transcript publishes that read.

The chip shows the token plan, which Models owns. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the plan read (the path was re-pointed when the models business moved into features/models/ in T03; the edge itself is unchanged).
The chip shows account usage, which Account owns. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes the usage read (T09 owns the account lifetime).
The rail labels a project by its workspace name, which the Workspace business derives. Reviewed peer edge until Workspace publishes the name projection.

Same read as the rail's, now from the grouping rule itself: T07 moved the project grouping into the sessions projection, so the name derivation is called where the group is built instead of in the surface that renders it. Reviewed peer edge until Workspace publishes the name projection; it then replaces the rail's entry too, since both readers take the published form.

The user menu opens the settings business's memory dialog. It is an Account surface opening a Settings surface; T12 moved the settings files into their feature home and re-pointed this entry. It goes when Settings publishes the dialog as a public contract.

The user menu opens the settings modal. It is an Account surface opening the settings composition; T12 moved the settings files into their feature home and re-pointed this entry. It goes when Settings publishes the open command as a public contract.

The workspace composer composes the review owner: the panels read one snapshot, and the review half is a peer business's owner. T11's acceptance says compose T10's review APIs rather than reimplementing review policy, and the owner factory is what there is to compose; the entry goes when review publishes a composition contract.

The review settings page lists the sessions it can review, reading the sessions catalogue. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes that read as a public contract (its owner moved into features/sessions in T07).
The panel renders file and diff content through the transcript's markdown renderer. Reviewed peer edge until the transcript publishes it as a shared rendering contract.
The review settings page renders the worktree surface's grouping for the sessions it reviews. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes that projection as a public contract.

The workspace panel hosts the terminal tab, so it measures the terminal grid. The plan keeps the terminal presented inside the workspace; the entry goes when T15 gives the terminal its own presentation attachment.

The transcript's diff card mounts the review business's turn-review binding to read a turn's diff. Before T10 the binding sat in `client/bindings/`, which the role rules classify as a home with no business, so the edge was not cross-business; moving it into the review business's own `bindings/` makes it one. Reviewed peer edge: the card renders review state, it does not own it, and the entry goes when review publishes the turn-diff read as a public contract the transcript can consume without its binding (T10).

The same binding, asked only whether the runtime offers turn diffs at all, so the card can be hidden rather than rendered empty. Same edge and same retirement as the DiffCard entry: review publishes the capability read as a public contract and this goes with it (T10).

The provider form is built from the settings surfaces' presentation atoms (IconButton, the close and refresh glyphs). Before T03 the form sat in `client/components/models/`, a current home the peer rule does not judge; moving it into the models feature home makes the edge measurable, and T12 moved the atoms into the settings feature home and re-pointed this entry. Reviewed peer edge while those atoms are filed under the settings business: they carry no settings policy, so the entry goes when T18 relocates the reusable presentation mechanics to `client/ui/`, or when settings publishes them.

The settings dialog renders the worktree surface's grouping for the archived-session settings page (the same projection the review settings page reads). Both files sat in current homes before T12 moved the dialog into the settings feature home, so the edge was not judged; reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes the worktree projection as a public contract.

The settings dialog composes the review business's settings page as one of its tabs. It is a Settings surface embedding a Review surface; reviewed peer edge until Review publishes that page as a public screen contract.

The settings dialog reads the account owner's snapshot through the account business's own binding (account status, sign-in and quota are setting-page resources that Account owns). Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes the status read as a public contract, or the dialog takes it as an injected view (T12's composition).

The archived-session settings page lists sessions from the sessions catalogue, the same read the review settings page makes. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes that read as a public contract (its owner moved into features/sessions in T07).

The usage/model-source screen shows the account's quota and credential status, read through the account business's own binding. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes the status read as a public contract.

The screen derives the active source badge, the provider header draft and the reset label through the models projection. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes that derivation (T03 owns the models surface).

The screen embeds the models business's provider form (provider CRUD is Models' duty, plan §5.6's models row, which this page renders rather than owns). Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the form as a public surface.

The goal projection reads the turn business's stream-message shape to recognise an already-recorded goal inside a streamed reply. Both files sat in the `projection/` layer before T05 moved goal into its feature home, so the edge was intra-layer; it becomes a reviewed peer edge until turn publishes that view type from its contracts.

The interaction coordinator holds the turn stream-phase command view rather than a stream writer (plan 5.2 interactions row: the transitions are invoked as turn's published commands). Those commands are declared by the sessions business's command module, which both owners sat beside before T05 moved interactions into its feature home. Reviewed peer edge until sessions publishes the command view as a public contract.

The session-keyed interaction owner applies the same session-scoped stream-phase commands after a questionnaire settles, for the same reason as the coordinator entry above. Reviewed peer edge until sessions publishes the command view as a public contract.

The plan decision card renders the plan text through the transcript's markdown renderer, the same shared rendering the workspace panel uses. Reviewed peer edge until the transcript publishes markdown as a shared rendering contract.

The composer's submit workflow enqueues through the turn business's queue command. Both sat in the application layer before T13 moved the composer owner; reviewed peer edge until turn publishes the queue command as a public contract.
The submit workflow reads the turn stream state to decide whether a send is a send or an enqueue. Reviewed peer edge until turn publishes that read from its contracts.
The same workflow composes the turn business's recovery policy when a send resumes after a stream error. Reviewed peer edge until turn publishes the recovery contract.
The workflow consumes the turn bundle the stream loop takes, the same bundle the session commands read. Reviewed peer edge until turn publishes it.

The composer's thinking trigger renders the models business's thinking-control projection (the control's vocabulary is Models', plan 5.2's models row). Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes that read.

The composer's project row hosts the workspace business's directory browser for the picker; T13 moved that row out of WebuiComposer into its own unit and the edge moved with it. Reviewed peer edge: the surface is Workspace's and the row only places it; it goes when Workspace publishes the picker.

The composer types its own plugin props (the catalogue object it reads from the owner and the installed-plugin list it holds) with the plugins business's Composer-facing shapes. Reviewed peer edge until Plugins publishes them from its contracts.

The composer's `+` menu lists the plugins business's Composer-facing catalogue (installed plugins and runtime skills) through the read model T08 published; T13 moved the menu out of WebuiComposer into its own unit and the edge moved with it. Reviewed peer edge until Plugins publishes it from its contracts.

The composer lists the child sessions of the session it composes for by resolving the sessions business's catalogue through its own selector; before T13 that list arrived as a page prop. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes the catalogue read from its contracts.

The composer reads the account business's live status to guard its own model scope against another session's value; before T13 that status arrived as an RPC prop the shell relayed. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes a binding the shell can mount.
The composer reads the transcript's message projection to build the pending-user/stream handoff shapes. Reviewed peer edge until the transcript publishes that read.
The composer types its sink against the interaction coordinator, the interaction view of the turn writer surface. Reviewed peer edge until interactions publishes the coordinator as a public contract.
The composer asks whether the selected model is a token-plan model, the same read the rail's chip makes. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the plan read.
The composer places the sessions business's context-usage chip beside its toolbar. Reviewed peer edge: the chip is Sessions' surface; it goes when Sessions publishes it.

The composer mounts the goal business's binding to reach its owner, because goal mode is entered from the composer while the owner is Goal's. Reviewed peer edge until Goal publishes a binding the shell can mount.
The composer mounts the interactions business's binding for the same reason as the goal one. Reviewed peer edge until interactions publishes a binding the shell can mount.
The composer reads the turn stream state for its live-column phase decisions. Reviewed peer edge until turn publishes the state as a public contract.
The composer renders the account usage label in its context chip; the label derivation is Account's. Reviewed peer edge until Account publishes that projection.
The composer places the goal business's banner above its own field. Reviewed peer edge: the banner is Goal's surface; it goes when Goal publishes it.
The composer places the interactions business's permission/questionnaire panel. Reviewed peer edge until interactions publishes the panel as a public surface.
The composer mounts the models business's picker: model choice is Models' owner and Models' surface. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes the picker.
The composer reads the models business's thinking-control rules for its toolbar control. Reviewed peer edge until Models publishes them.
The composer renders the transcript's output-error surface under its field. Reviewed peer edge until the transcript publishes it as a shared surface.

The composer builds session commands (fork / edit / rewind) with the sessions business's builders, the same ones the transcript's message actions use. Reviewed peer edge until Sessions publishes the command shape.

The composer's project row labels the workspace with the workspace business's name derivation; T13 moved that row out of WebuiComposer into its own unit and the edge moved with it. Reviewed peer edge until Workspace publishes the name projection.
